title: finding(scripts): the `vite-objectstack-spec-dist` browser-arm pin is 39/41 against a spec built from objectstack main — the arm moved from `./cloud` to `./api`, and the shape gate is COMPILER-BLIND to it
body:
`scripts/__tests__/vite-objectstack-spec-dist.test.ts` pins **which `exports` entries of `@objectstack/spec` carry a `browser` arm**. On objectstack `main` that set has moved — the browser arm left `./cloud` and appeared on `./api` — so **2 of its 41 assertions fail** against a `main`-built spec while all 41 pass against the pinned published 17.4.0.

⚠️ ⛔ This is invisible to the objectui#9860 shape gate: an `exports` map is a **package.json fact**, ⛔ not a type, so `tsc` cannot see it. The gate is green on this and the pin is the only instrument that catches it.

## The measurement

Reported by the `os-dev` on objectui#9860, two legs, **same file, same command**, differing only in which `@objectstack/spec` was injected into `node_modules`:

| injected spec | result |
|:--|--:|
| published `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0` | **41 / 41 pass** |
| built from objectstack `main` | **39 / 41** — 2 failures in this one file |

⭐ The two legs are what make this a measurement rather than a flaky-test report: the same tree, the same invocation, one variable.

⚠️ This also explains an earlier reading on that card that would otherwise look like a regression: a `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/` run showed 2 failures in this file, and with the published spec restored the same suite is **exit 0, 174 files / 5173 tests**. ⇒ ⛔ the diff never broke it; the injected spec did.

## Why it needs a card rather than a note

The drift is **real and upstream**, and today nothing surfaces it until someone bumps the `@objectstack/spec` pin — at which point this pin goes red **at the bump** rather than **at the drift**, in a PR whose author did not cause it. ⚠️ That is the late-discovery shape, ⛔ not a false alarm: the pin is doing its job, just at the worst moment.

First deliverable is the judgement, ⛔ not a re-run:
1. Is the `./cloud` → `./api` browser-arm move **intended** upstream (in which case the pin's expected set is what must move, and the card is a one-line update riding the pin bump), or is it **drift** (in which case it belongs upstream)?
2. Should the browser-arm set be pinned by **enumeration** at all, or derived — the same question objectui#9871 asks about the `body`-dialect producer table.

⚠️ ⛔ The filing seat answers neither. It measured the two legs and stopped.

## Dedupe words

- `vite-objectstack-spec-dist browser arm exports`
- `spec exports map cloud api browser`
- `39 of 41 spec main exports pin`
- `exports-map drift compiler-invisible`
